facts.evidence: **Net income** of **$21.2 billion** ($7.70 per share), up **41%** YoY
**return on tangible common equity (ROTCE)** of **29%**, and **ROTCE excluding significant items** of **23%**
including **$4.6 billion** in net gains related to Visa shares and **$1.0 billion** in gains on equity investments
**Capital distributions** included a **$4.0 billion** common dividend and **$6.2 billion** in common stock repurchases
**Basel III CET1 capital ratios** of **14.1% (standardized)** and **14.2% (advanced)**

claims.claim: Net income was $21.2 billion.
Earnings per share were $7.70.
Net income was up 41% year over year.
Results included $4.6 billion in net gains related to Visa shares.
Results included $1.0 billion in gains on certain equity investments.
Managed revenue was $58.0 billion, up 27% year over year.
Net interest income was $25.6 billion, up 10% year over year.
Noninterest revenue was $32.4 billion, up 45% year over year.
Return on common equity was 24%.
Return on tangible common equity was 29%.
ROTCE excluding significant items was 23%.
Credit costs were $2.5 billion.
Net charge-offs were $2.4 billion.
There was a $149 million net reserve build.
Average loans were up 10% year over year.
Average loans were $1.5 trillion.
Average deposits were up 7% year over year.
Average deposits were $1.5 trillion.
claims.note: The release gives no average deposit balance. The $1.5T figures in the release are average loans and cash and marketable securities; the brief attaches the loan balance to deposits.

claims.claim: Cash and marketable securities were $1.5 trillion.
CCB net income was $5.3 billion, up 3% year over year.
CCB Card Services & Auto revenue was up 12% year over year.
The Card Services & Auto revenue increase was due to higher revolving balances and higher auto operating lease income.
CIB net income was $9.7 billion, up 46% year over year.
Markets revenue was up 35% year over year.
Equity Markets revenue was up 86% year over year.
Investment Banking fees were up 30% year over year.
Investment Banking fees reached their highest level since 2021.
AWM net income was $2.0 billion, up 33% year over year.
Assets under management were $5.1 trillion, up 18% year over year.
There were $50 billion of long-term AUM net inflows.
Corporate net income was $4.2 billion, up $2.5 billion year over year.
The Corporate result was driven by $4.5 billion in noninterest revenue excluding significant items.
claims.note: Misapplies the figure and basis. The $4.5 billion is the YoY increase in Corporate net revenue on a reported basis; excluding significant items Corporate net revenue was DOWN $805 million. Corporate noninterest revenue was $5.2 billion, up $5.2 billion, or down $138 million excluding significant items. The release attributes the Corporate net income change to lower net interest income and the absence of a prior-year $774 million tax benefit.

claims.claim: The $4.6 billion of Visa-related gains was recorded in Corporate.
The release provides no explicit guidance.
Dimon described a particularly favorable environment with an elevated level of market activity.
Dimon highlighted risks including geopolitical tensions, sticky inflation and large global fiscal deficits.
Dimon cited rigorous execution, years of consistent investment and thoughtful capital deployment as drivers of performance.
The Basel III Standardized CET1 ratio was 14.1%.
The Basel III Advanced CET1 ratio was 14.2%.
Total loss-absorbing capacity was $590 billion.
Standardized RWA were $2.1 trillion.
Book value per share was $133.01, up 9% year over year.
Tangible book value per share was $113.35, up 10% year over year.
The common dividend was $4.0 billion.
Common stock repurchases were $6.2 billion.
The net payout ratio over the last twelve months was 73%.
Net reserve builds remain elevated.
claims.note: Contradicted by the release: the firmwide net reserve build was $149 million versus $439 million in the prior-year quarter, and CCB reserves were flat. Reserve builds declined year over year.

claims.claim: Fixed Income Markets revenue grew 6% year over year.
Net interest income excluding Markets grew 4%.
The 4% growth in net interest income excluding Markets reflects the impact of lower rates.
